problem_summary.summary: Search for a target in a strictly increasing array that may have been rotated, returning its index or -1.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: a possibly rotated integer array nums with distinct values and target. Return the target index, or -1 when absent.
constraints: nums is an ascending array that may be rotated
The required algorithm runs in O(log n) time

brute_force.explanation: Scan each array position and return the index whose value equals target. If no position matches, return -1.
brute_force.correctness_idea: Every possible location is checked, so the scan returns the unique matching index if present and correctly reports absence otherwise.

optimized.explanation: At each binary-search step, at least one half is sorted. Check whether target lies within that half's inclusive value range; keep that half if it does, otherwise search the other half.
optimized.correctness_idea: Distinct values ensure one half around mid is strictly sorted. Range membership in that half determines whether it can contain target; excluding the other half cannot discard a match. The remaining interval therefore keeps the target if present.
optimized.time_complexity: O(log n), where n is nums.length.

steps.condition: nums[left] > nums[mid], so the right half [2, 5] is sorted. Target 4 lies in [2, 5].
steps.action: Keep the right half by setting left to mid + 1.

edge_cases.handling: The loop returns 0 on a match and -1 otherwise.
The ordinary sorted-half range check still narrows correctly.
The candidate interval becomes empty and the method returns -1.
Inclusive endpoint checks retain the half that can contain it.
